title: Partner onboarding slate: demo scenarios and shipcheck
body:
Purpose: quick, low-friction runbook for onboarding a marketplace partner bundle (SMB-focused SKU) that covers demo dialogue, acceptance QA, and a final shipcheck. This is intentionally lean — meant for AE/SE + partner PM to use during the last 7 days before listing.

Background/context:
- Target listing: SMB Bundle (trial + metered usage) in AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace.
- Primary audience: product managers at ISV partner, partner sales engineers, our partner success manager.
- Goal: reduce manual back-and-forth at publish time; provide canonical demo flow + acceptance checklist so marketplace publishing is predictable.

Quick elevator copy (for partner tile):
- Headline (short): "Redwood Inference: Fast, predictable LLM inference"
- Two-line: "Deploy inference that scales with predictable latency and cost. Dedicated and private options with enterprise SLAs."
- CTA variants (choose one): "Start free trial", "Request a demo", "Get started — 14 days free"
- Long description bullets (use in listing long-form):
  • High-throughput inference tuned for production LLM apps (text, chat, embeddings).
  • Dedicated capacity and private deployment options for regulated workloads.
  • Built-in cost controls: batching, quantization suggestions, and KV caching.
  • Enterprise features: SSO, KMS, audit logs, SLA-backed latency targets.

Demo scenarios (3 canonical flows — keep each ~3–5 minutes in live demo):
1) Quickstart: "API in 3 minutes"
   - Objective: show how to provision a hosted API key and make a generation call.
   - Steps: create account (demo org), navigate to hosted API quickstart, copy curl command, run sample prompt that returns structured JSON.
   - Success signals: API key issued, first token returned in <2s, sample response formatted as JSON with expected fields.
   - Troubles: if creation hangs, show how to use partner sandbox key (ticket: GMKT-4118).

2) Predictable latency for a user-facing chat app
   - Objective: demonstrate latency guarantees and fallback.
   - Steps: show baseline call to production model (p99 latency), then switch to lower-cost quantized variant via routing policy and show graceful degradation.
   - Success signals: latency change reflected in console, latency telemetry appears in monitoring within 30s.
   - Talking points: how routing policies reduce cost without user-visible interruptions.

3) Private deployment demo (VPC brief and provisioning checklist)
   - Objective: reassure enterprise buyers about private option and KMS integration.
   - Steps: show VPC onboarding doc, basic SAML SSO flow, and KMS key mapping screenshot.
   - Success signals: SSO login successful, KMS key visible in console, customer-managed logs present.

Demo scripts / SE copilot text (short snippets you can paste into demo):
- Intro line: "We designed Redwood for teams that need predictable latency and clear unit economics — you'll see both in this demo."
- When showing routing: "Notice how we route lower-priority traffic to a quantized model; critical traffic stays on the higher-fidelity model."
- On security: "Your keys remain in your KMS and we never store raw inputs outside of your retention policy."

Acceptance QA checklist (marketplace / publisher gating tests):
- Legal / commercial:
  • Marketplace contract uploaded and signed (doc id).
  • SKU mapping verified vs billing matrix (link to internal SKU sheet).
- Technical / runtime:
  • Sandbox image and public demo endpoint validated (curl + sample prompt).
  • Health checks return 200 for /health and /metrics endpoints.
  • Provisioning time for trial account <= 5 minutes.
- Security / compliance:
  • SSO (SAML) smoke test completed, at least one IdP tested (Okta).
  • KMS/HSM integration tested, encryption-at-rest verified.
  • Audit logs flow to partner workspace with 30-day retention (or per agreement).
- Observability / telemetry:
  • Console shows per-model p50/p95/p99 latency for 1k sample requests.
  • Cost estimation tile appears and matches expected per-token cost within 20%.
- UX / copy acceptance:
  • Marketplace tile headline passes character limits for AWS/Azure.
  • Short description contains no trademark violations and aligns with legal copy.
  • 2–3 screenshots for listing uploaded (tile, console, demo chat).

Shipcheck (final 24–48 hour pre-publish run):
- Confirm legal sign-off and SKU activation. (owner: partner-legal + GMKT lead)
- Confirm billing test charge processed for test account.
- Confirm automated smoke tests run against publisher endpoint (CI job: partner-smoke-main).
- Confirm pub-locale copy checks: EN-US done, EN-GB pass review.
- Confirm monitoring alert integrations: slack channel #marketplace-publish has subscription to alerts.
- Lockdown: freeze doc edits to listing copy (owner: GMKT copy lead).

Sample risk & rollback notes (short):
- Risk: billing metering mismatch on launch day.
  • Rollback: unpublish tile, pause buyer access, coordinate with marketplace billing team (on-call: finance-billing).
- Risk: data residency misconfiguration.
  • Rollback: disable Private deployment option, notify customer, escalate to infra SRE.

Unresolved questions (to call out in partner kickoff):
- Which SKU will be the default for new signups? (partner PM)
- Confirm trial length and transition to paid — auto-convert or opt-in? (growth + legal)
- SLA badge level for tile (bronze/silver/gold) and associated copy.

Pointers / quick links for SEs during demo:
- Demo sandbox key: slack #gm-demo-keys (pinned message)
- Preflight CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/partner-smoke/actions
- Relevant tickets: GMKT-4120 (listing acceptance), GMKT-4118 (sandbox key fallback)

Notes to self / rough TODOs (informal):
- Pull screenshots from console with newest latency UI (ask infra-monitoring team).
- Draft final UX tile copy to meet AWS 120-char short desc limit.
- Run through demo script with Miguel / Benji 48 hours before publish.

Slack snippets you can copy to partner to confirm readiness:
- "Hey — final shipcheck scheduled for Thu 9am PT. Please confirm legal signoff and screenshots uploaded by Wed EOD."
- "Quick ask: can you confirm the default SKU for trial auto-convert? We need to map billing SKU before publish."

Appendix: character limits & asset specs (quick)
- AWS short description: 120 chars; long description: 4000 chars; tile image: 1200x628 PNG.
- Azure tile: title 100 chars; description 3000 chars; image 1024x512.

If you use this doc: copy to partner folder (partner-specific naming), fill the unresolved questions section, and paste the demo scripts into the meeting agenda. This should remove a lot of back-and-forth on launch day.

End of runbook — feedback welcome (drop notes in thread: #gm-marketplace-ops).
